proposed.text: An architect created a design in 1999 and died in 2010. Under RA 8293 Section 213.1, when does copyright protection for this individual-author work expire?

options.text: In 2005 (20 years after creation), which is incorrect as copyright duration is based on the creator's lifetime
In 2035 (25 years after creation), which does not apply as the protection extends beyond the creator's lifetime
In 2060 (50 years after the architect's death)
In 2070 (60 years after the architect's death), which is a common misconception about copyright duration

rationale.b: This uses the applied-art period instead of the individual-author term stated in Section 213.1.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 213.1 protects works under Sections 172 and 173 during the life of the author and for fifty years after death. The architect died in 2010, so protection runs 50 years after death, to 2060. The 1999 creation date does not control the individual-author term.
rationale.takeaway: For individual-author works, calculate from the author's death, not the creation date.
